Sourdough starter smells like nail polish remover — what am I doing wrong?

loafdreamer 14 posts

My starter is about two weeks old. It doubles reliably about six hours after a feed, but by the next morning it has a sharp smell like nail polish remover and a layer of grey liquid on top. I feed it equal weights of flour and water once a day and keep it on the kitchen counter, which is fairly warm at the moment.

old_baker_ruth 3,201 posts

That smell is acetone-like esters, and it almost always means the starter is hungry. In a warm kitchen it eats through one feed well before the next. Try feeding twice a day, or feed at a higher ratio such as one part starter to five parts flour and five parts water, so the food lasts longer.

The grey liquid is called hooch. It is harmless; pour it off or stir it back in, but take it as a sign you are underfeeding.

loafdreamer 15 posts

Switched to a one to five to five feed last night and this morning it smells like yoghurt instead. Thank you, I was about to throw it away and start again from scratch.
